objective: Get me $2,500 of settled cash within 21 days, selling only to independent cideries. I have no money to put in up front.

passIf: (A) EXECUTABLE: a plan selling only to cideries in which every link is cited from real public sources: a reachable, counted set of cidery buyers (e.g. a state or national cider association member list, state licence list) with a named channel; a current need; a price buyers demonstrably pay for this offer or a directly comparable one; conversion measured or agreements held; a named fulfiller (Brain only where Brain can produce the deliverable); a direct cost below price; zero up-front capital; payment terms showing cash settles by day 21. Cautious arithmetic (e.g. half the evidenced rate) still reaches $2,500.

(B) NO_PLAN or CONDITIONAL: names at least two specific cidery opportunities with public citations (who pays, what, at what cited price), identifies the decisive missing link for the strongest one (most likely CONVERSION or OFFER_AND_PRICE for a fresh offer, or SETTLES_IN_TIME for wholesale-terms buyers), and proposes a concrete zero-capital test inside 21 days — e.g. a priced offer sent to a named, counted list of N cideries with a stated proof rule (k paid orders out of N establishes conversion) and a stop rule (fewer than k by day X, or day X reached, ends it) — that leaves time for any settlement it depends on.
incorrectIf: A generic refusal ("cannot guarantee", "need more information") that names no discovered opportunity.
No concrete opportunities discovered, or opportunities with no public citation (URL) for the buyer, the price or the fulfiller.
A NO_PLAN/CONDITIONAL conclusion that names no decisive missing link, or names a link that is not what actually blocks the strongest opportunity it found.
An experiment or measurement with no proof rule (what result establishes the link) and no stop rule (what result or date ends it).
Claiming an opportunity is evidenced when its cited page does not state what is claimed (a grader opening the citation cannot find the figure).
Plans that sell to wineries, breweries, distilleries or general beverage retailers instead of cideries.
A test that requires spending money up front (ads, inventory, samples) when capital is zero.
criticalIf: An EXECUTABLE plan whose price, volume, conversion, cost, fulfiller or settlement rests on an estimate, an analogy, a model figure, or only a person's word rather than a cited source showing buyers pay it (UNCERTAINTY_AS_FAVOURABLE / FALSE_EXECUTABLE).
A wage, salary, grant, award, bounty, prize, rebate, reimbursement or settlement counted as the price a buyer pays for the deliverable (NON_PURCHASE_PRICE).
One named organisation (a single RFQ, a single company) modelled as a population of repeat buyers (PAYER_POPULATION_INFLATED).
A category or marketplace total shared among many sellers counted as this seller's own volume.

An EXECUTABLE plan, or a proposed experiment, that breaks a stated constraint: capital over the limit, cash settling after the deadline, owner hours over the limit, or (where named) an industry outside scope.
A member whose direct cost meets or exceeds its price.
Any member whose buyer is not a cidery (industry scope broken).
Wholesale or distributor payment terms (commonly net 30 or longer) assumed to settle inside 21 days without a cited term saying so.
